name: Defensible Space / Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design
citation: Newman, O. (1972). Defensible space. Macmillan. / Jeffery, C.R. (1971). Crime prevention through environmental design. Sage.
rejection_rationale: Confounded by social variables (Merry, 1981 critique). Defensible Space/CPTED claims about environmental design reducing crime cannot be separated from the social dynamics of the communities inhabiting those spaces. The Pruitt-Igoe failure was social-economic, not architectural. Template coverage would require sociological variables outside the neural-mechanistic framework.
key_references: Merry, S.E. (1981). Defensible space undefended. Urban Affairs Quarterly, 16(4), 397-422.

function_form.function_form: Crime(x) = f(Opportunity(x), Guardianship(x), Target(x)); Guardianship ∝ Surveillance + Territoriality
predictions: Natural surveillance (windows facing public space) reduces crime ~25-30%
Territorial markers (fences, landscaping) reduce stranger intrusion ~40%
